Put on a hat! You lose half your body heat through your head. Except, you don't.
This idea comes from old military experiments in the nineteen fifties.
People were bundled up in warm clothes, but their heads were left uncovered.

text: Of course most heat escaped through the head. It was the only part sticking out!

An army field manual even claimed forty to forty-five percent.

text: Wait. So how much is it really?

You see, your head is only about seven percent of your skin.
And according to the British Medical Journal, it loses about seven to ten percent of your heat. Pretty much its fair share.
Go outside in shorts, and your legs would lose way more.

text: So yes, wear the hat. But maybe also wear pants.
